title: Shannon capacity of \(C_{7}\)
formal: Determine \(\Theta (C_{7})=\sup _{t\ge 1} \alpha\)(\(C_{7}\)^{⊠t})^\(\{1/t\}\), the zero-error Shannon capacity of the seven-cycle, where the graph power and independence number are defined below.
context:
Shannon capacity measures how many mutually distinguishable messages can be encoded across repeated uses of a confusability graph. Distinct input tuples may be confused only if every coordinate is identical or adjacent in the graph. Joint coding can therefore improve on selecting an independent set in one use.

The seven-cycle is the first unresolved odd cycle after the pentagon. The saved 2026 source develops lower-bound constructions and reports a remaining gap for odd cycles; this formulation review does not independently verify its proofs. The card concerns this one numerical capacity, while the related computability question quantifies over arbitrary graphs.
why: The smallest odd-cycle zero-error capacity left unresolved after Lovasz's pentagon theorem.

sentences: The seven-cycle describes which pairs of seven channel symbols can be confused.
Its Shannon capacity is the supremum of independence numbers of strong graph powers raised to the reciprocal power.
The card asks for this real number in distinguishable symbols per use, rather than bits per use.
No finite graph power is assumed to attain the supremum.
The Lean benchmark accepts an explicit value with certified absolute error at most 0.01.

definitions: \(C_{7}\) has vertex set \(\{0,\ldots ,6\}\), with distinct vertices adjacent when their difference modulo 7 is 1 or 6. For an integer \(t\ge 1\), the strong power has vertex set \(\{0,\ldots ,6\}^{t}\). Two distinct tuples are adjacent when, in every coordinate, their entries are equal or adjacent in \(C_{7}\). An independent set contains no adjacent distinct pair, and \(\alpha\) is its maximum cardinality. The capacity is measured in distinguishable symbols per channel use, rather than its logarithm in bits. It lies between 3 and 7; the supremum need not occur at a finite power. There is no computational restriction on independent sets or their construction.
answer_criterion: Supply a specified real number a and prove in Lean that |\(a- \Theta (C_{7})|\le 1/100\). The proof must certify both a lower and an upper bound for the unrestricted quantity in this card. Equivalently, certified bounds \(\ell\)\(\le u\) of width at most \(1/50\) qualify by taking \(a=(\ell +u)/2\). An exact value with proof of equality also qualifies. An unevaluated copy of the defining extremum, a one-sided improvement, or a numerical estimate without a proved error bound does not meet this criterion. The \(1/100\) tolerance is benchmark acceptance; it does not prove an associated exact threshold conjecture.
